sections.h2: Who to call about a Haywood County tax bill
sections.html:
Two offices in the Historic Haywood Courthouse in Waynesville split the work, both at 215 N. Main Street. The Tax Assessor's Office sets values and sits in Suite 220. Tax Collections mails bills and takes payments from Suite 224.

Call Collections at 828-452-6643 about partial payments or the amount needed to clear a parcel before a sale. The assessor's reappraisal line is 828-452-6734.

Your bill may include more than the county rate. The county collects for 22 fire districts, 10 road maintenance districts and one sanitation district. Owners of improved property, manufactured homes and campers included, also pay a landfill fee.

Haywood had about 63,369 residents in its July 2025 estimate, up 2.1% since 2020, with 36,637 housing units. About 74.9% are owner-occupied, and the median owner-occupied value is $279,200.

Bills go out in late August or early September and are expected in September. Nothing accrues through January 5. After that day a 2% charge applies, then 3/4% more at the start of each month until the account is cleared.

Haywood County property tax calendar
DateWhat happens
January 1Who owns a parcel is determined for the tax year
Late August to early SeptemberBills mailed to owners
SeptemberTaxes due
January 5Last day without interest
After January 52% charge, then 3/4% monthly
MarchUnpaid real estate taxes advertised with a fee added

If you cannot clear a bill by January 5, ask Collections about a fixed monthly payment. The statewide interest rule is in G.S. 105-360.

You can pay on the website, by phone at 1-877-729-8290, by mail, in a dropbox outside the Historic Courthouse, or in cash at the Collections counter. A processor, not the county, charges 3% on cards (online or by phone) and 2% on e-checks.

  • The dropbox takes checks and money orders only. Never leave cash in it.
  • Mail goes to the address on the bill. The county changed its lockbox to PO Box 96270, Charlotte. A returned payment can be resent to the Waynesville office in its original envelope, which keeps the first postmark.
  • The county sends no bills to lenders or escrow companies. If your mortgage servicer pays the tax, forward your copy to them.

sections.h2: Why was the revaluation moved to 2027?
sections.html:
After Hurricane Helene, Haywood pushed its reappraisal back two years, from 2025 to January 1, 2027, after confirming with the state that the delay was allowed.

Until then, most parcels keep their 2025 values unless something changed, such as an addition, an update, new construction or flooding. The 2027 numbers will follow the market as it stands then, which could move a Waynesville or Maggie Valley assessment a long way.

Commissioners set the schedule of values, standards and rules for 2027 after a public hearing, and the schedules can be viewed in the second-floor assessor's office. State law requires reappraisal at least every eighth year, as written in G.S. 105-286.

Fill out the county's Damage Report Form and send it to the assessor in person, by post, or to personalproperty@haywoodcountync.gov. If your house flooded, do this so the assessment reflects its current condition before you list it.

Value disputes on real property go to the county's review board, which has five appointed members and one alternate serving one-year terms. The assessor schedules its meetings as the need arises.

  • Ask to be heard before adjournment, as G.S. 105-322 requires.
  • Expect the written result within a month of adjournment.
  • File any Property Tax Commission appeal within thirty days of the board's mailed notice.

Three state programs cover a permanent residence, and an owner can use only one. With 28.2% of residents 65 or over, the age-based ones reach many Haywood homeowners. File Form AV-9 with the assessor.

  • Owners 65 or older, or disabled, can shelter half the value or $25,000, whichever is larger, if income is at or under $38,800 for 2026.
  • A veteran with a permanent and total service-connected disability shelters $45,000 of value.
  • The circuit breaker caps tax at a share of income (4.0% or 5.0%) after five years in the home and defers the rest.

Applications are due in the January listing period but are accepted through June 1. A deferral ends on transfer, so it becomes a closing item when you sell.

Foreclosure can begin any day after January 5 of the collection year. The county says it forecloses only when an owner does not respond or breaks a payment arrangement. Before that, the collector can attach bank accounts, garnish wages or rents, or levy on personal property.

Two routes exist. In an in-rem foreclosure under G.S. 105-375, the Tax Department and County Attorney handle everything. In a mortgage-style case under G.S. 105-374, an outside attorney does. Sales are public auctions in front of the Haywood County Justice Center, as is and without warranty. The buyer puts down 20% and owes the balance at the end of the 10-day period and confirmation. Upset bids must exceed the last bid by 5%, at least $750, and are filed with the Clerk of Superior Court.

Selling does not erase the year's bill. Ownership is fixed on January 1, so a mid-year transfer leaves the seller liable and the payoff is settled at closing.

sections.h2: Steps for selling with taxes due
sections.html:
Call Tax Collections at 828-452-6643 first and ask for the amount needed to clear the parcel. Give that figure to your closing attorney so the payoff comes out of the sale proceeds. If you have a deferral under the circuit breaker, expect it to come due at transfer, so ask Collections for that number too.

If your house was damaged, send the Damage Report Form to the assessor before listing. A buyer will want to see an assessment that matches the house. A cash buyer who skips repairs and appraisals can close without waiting on any of this, but the tax payoff is still settled at the table.

Timing changes what you owe. A house sold in October still carries the full year's bill in the seller's name, because ownership was fixed on January 1. Bills are mailed in late August or early September, so a seller who closes in the fall may get the bill after the sale and should forward it to the closing attorney. If the bill goes unpaid past January 5, interest starts, and by March the parcel can be advertised with a fee added.

faqs.q: When does interest start on Haywood County property tax?
faqs.a: After January 5. The county adds 2% then, and a further three-quarters of one percent at the start of each month until the bill is paid.

faqs.q: Does Haywood County sell tax lien certificates?
faqs.a: No. The county says North Carolina does not sell tax liens or tax certificates over the counter. Paying someone else's delinquent bill does not transfer ownership.

faqs.q: When is the next Haywood County revaluation?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027. The county moved it from 2025 after Hurricane Helene, and most 2025 values stay in place unless the property changed.

faqs.q: I sold my house, so why did I get the tax bill?
faqs.a: Ownership of real property is set as of January 1 of the tax year, and a transfer during the year does not remove the seller's liability. Settle the year's tax at closing.

faqs.q: Where do I send storm damage reports?
faqs.a: To the Tax Assessor's Office at 215 N. Main Street, Suite 220, Waynesville, NC 28786, or by email to personalproperty@haywoodcountync.gov, using the Damage Report Form.
